_comment: Copy to config.json and edit for your booth. Nothing secret belongs in git; secrets go in .env (see .env.example).

build._comment: shapeSizes are the backing bounding boxes in mm; kept modest so prints stay under the 15-min budget. customMax bounds the free-draw shape.
build._square_comment: Corner radius of the square backing, in mm. A right angle is sharp in a pocket and is also the first corner to lift off the bed.
build._outline_comment: Freehand custom-shape healing. outlineCloseMm bridges the gap where the loop didn't quite close; outlineOpenMm deletes spikes/needles thinner than about twice this; outlineSmooth is Chaikin smoothing passes.
build._image_comment: Importing a PNG/JPEG drawing (studios upload instead of drawing live). The browser decodes and thresholds it; these control what the engine does with the resulting bitmap, and are the numbers to tune against REAL sample uploads — a clean black-on-white export and a phone photo of pencil are different problems. imageCloseMm bridges the pin-holes threshold speckle leaves in a fill. imageSpeckMm drops any blob smaller than a dot of this diameter (a dust speck on a photo), by area, so thin lines are kept. imageMinFeatureMm is the printable minimum: anything thinner is thickened up to it rather than printed as a whisker that snaps off. All in mm.
build._imageMinFeature_comment: 0.5, NOT the 0.8 of penRange — they answer different questions. penRange[0] is the thinnest pen a child is offered, so a deliberate hand-drawn line reads as a line. This is the thinnest bead the printer will hold at all, a shade over one 0.45mm line width. Scanned line art is full of detail between the two, and rounding it all up to 0.8 turns a face into a blot. Raise it if imported drawings come off the plate with lines missing or snapped.
build._stroke_comment: strokeSmooth is Chaikin passes over the drawn points. strokeStepMm is how far apart the bead points end up: the line is laid along a spline at this spacing, so smoothness stops depending on how fast the child moved their hand. Smaller is smoother and makes a bigger file; below about 0.3 there is nothing left to see.
build._wall_comment: wallLoops: number of perimeters (Bambu default 2). infillWallOverlap: fraction of a line width the infill reaches into the innermost wall, which prevents a groove at the edges.

speed._comment: mm/min. topSurface is the visible last layer: solid fill turns every line width, and at solidInfill speed the nozzle never reaches the commanded speed before braking for the next turn, so flow varies through every turn. Slower there buys a cleaner top for a few seconds.
speed._maxVolumetricMmps: THE speed limit that matters. The A1 mini's motion system will happily run 250 mm/s; its hotend can only melt about 12 mm3 of PLA per second, and this is the number Bambu Studio enforces for this printer (filament_max_volumetric_speed = 12). Every extruding move is slowed to fit, so the speeds above are aspirations and this is the ceiling. Raise it only if you fit a higher-flow hotend; lower it (8-10) if prints still look under-melted. 0 turns the cap off — don't.

calibration._comment: Runs once per print, before the prime line. A full G29 mesh probe costs over a minute — on a 13-minute keychain that is a tenth of the booth's throughput, for every kid. Off means the printer uses the mesh it stored the last time it levelled: level once on arrival from the printer's own screen, or turn bedLevel on for the day's first print. startupMinutes/bedLevelMinutes only feed the time estimate.

limits._comment: These went up when the volumetric cap went in. The old 15/13 were measured against files that asked the hotend for twice what it can melt — the estimate was honest arithmetic about a print that then failed. A keychain that finishes takes about 15 minutes, so the budget is 18. To buy time back, thin the plate (build.backingThickness) or drop build.solidLayers to 1 — not by raising speed.maxVolumetricMmps, which is what caused the failures.

colourChange._comment: The filament swap at the backing->design transition, shaped like Bambu Studio's 'multi-colour with external spool': park clear, back the old colour out of the melt zone, pause for the swap, then purge and wipe the new colour so the drawing does not start in the old one. Set mode to 'pause' for a bare M400 U1 and let the printer's filament menu handle it. Setting a 'gcode' array replaces the whole block.
colourChange._mode_comment: "purge" (default) parks, retracts and pauses — the operator works the printer's filament menu to unload and load. "bambu" emits the A1 mini's OWN change sequence, transcribed from Bambu Studio's machine profile: it drives the head into the cutter, snips, unloads, asks for the new spool on the printer screen, and feeds it until the extruder gear catches — what you get slicing a two-colour print with an external spool. It uses undocumented Bambu commands (G392/M620.x/T255/M628/M629), so WATCH THE FIRST ONE before trusting it to a queue of children. "cut" is the middle ground and the one to reach for first: it cuts and pulls the old colour out — the fiddly half, and the half that has been seen to work — then pauses so you load the new one from the printer's filament menu. "pause" is a bare M400 U1.
colourChange._bambu_comment: Only used when mode is "bambu". cutX is where the cutter lives — 180 is the right-hand edge of the A1 mini's 180mm bed and is taken from Bambu's own A1 mini profile. Do NOT copy an A1 (non-mini) value here; the bed is a different size and the head would be driven into the frame. cutRetractMm is Bambu's retraction_distances_when_cut. flushMmps defaults to speed.maxVolumetricMmps.
colourChange._tool_comment: Which filament the change switches INTO, as an index into this print's own filament list: 0 is the first colour, 1 is the second. Read out of a real Bambu Studio two-colour export for an A1 mini with NO AMS attached, which changes with "M620 S1A" / "T1". NOT 254 and NOT 255 — both were reasoned out rather than read, and cost six prints. 255 appears only in the end-of-print unload.
colourChange._amsFraming_comment: Whether M620/M621 carry the "A" suffix. It is NOT AMS addressing, which is what we assumed for a long time: the no-AMS export writes S1A / S0A on every change. Leave it true. false only exists to reproduce the old behaviour when comparing against an earlier print.
colourChange._flush_comment: flushTemp is the nozzle temperature the purge runs at. Bambu uses the HIGHEST of the two filaments rather than the printing temperature, so the old colour clears instead of leaving a plug behind. flushLenMm is the L parameter on M620.10 — the slicer computes it per change from its flush-volume matrix; 342 is what it used for a black-to-light change.
pauseGcode: M400 U1 ; ===== SWAP THE FILAMENT NOW, then press Resume on the printer =====
colourChange._purge_comment: parkX/parkY put the nozzle clear of the part while it purges — 180,90 is the right-hand edge, which is where Bambu's own file purges. purgeMm is how much new filament to push through before printing with it; a dark colour needs less to cover, a light one after a dark one needs more. TEST THIS ONCE and watch where the purge lands before relying on it.

template._comment: Replace start.gcode / end.gcode with the header+footer from a REAL sliced A1 mini file for your filament, so bed levelling / flow calibration run correctly. Placeholders {nozzle} {bed} {nozzleFirst} {bedFirst} are substituted.

_eventName_comment: Shown on the kiosk welcome screen and sent with every lead. Name the event, the school or the studio — this software is not tied to any one of them.

output._comment: Where the day's files land. Both accept an absolute path, so they can point at a synced or backup folder while the booth itself runs from local disk — do NOT run the project from inside Google Drive/OneDrive/Dropbox, which sync node_modules and .git file by file and lock them mid-write. e.g. "dir": "G:/My Drive/3DiPad/gcode"

operator._comment: The send-to-printer panel on the kiosk. The PIN stops a child who has worked out the hold — it is not security, and anyone on the booth Wi-Fi can still reach the API. Leave "pin" empty for no PIN (the hold alone). Put the real one in .env as BOOTH_ADMIN_PIN if you would rather it were not in a file you edit at the booth.

notify._comment: Who sends the WhatsApp: 'ghl' (GoHighLevel inbound webhook — recommended, GHL owns the message + nurture), 'meta' (direct WhatsApp Cloud API, see whatsapp block), or 'none'.

ghl._comment: Inbound-webhook URLs go in .env (GHL_LEAD_WEBHOOK_URL / GHL_READY_WEBHOOK_URL) or here. One URL is fine — branch on payload.event in the GHL workflow.

lan._comment: Bambu LAN-mode auto-send + status monitoring. On each printer turn ON both LAN Mode AND DEVELOPER MODE (Settings > Network), then restart it and copy the Access Code + Serial below. Developer Mode is the one that is easy to miss: without it the printer reports status, obeys the light and accepts uploads, but refuses every print command with err_code 0x05024007 — files reach the SD card and nothing ever starts. The setup page tests for this.
lan._dispatch_comment: autoDispatch false means a submitted design waits in the queue until an operator presses a printer's button on the dashboard. Each printer holds particular filament, so picking the machine is a decision about colour. Set true only if every printer carries the same two colours.
lan._qos_comment: The printer does not acknowledge MQTT publishes, so the start command goes out at QoS 0 and whether it worked is read from the printer's own reported state. startConfirmMs is how long to give it to turn over before saying it never started; maxDispatchAttempts stops a switched-off printer from spinning the whole queue.
lan._container_comment: What actually goes on the SD card. Bambu Studio never sends bare g-code — it sends a 3mf project with the g-code inside at Metadata/plate_1.gcode, and the printer's own task record points at a .3mf. Uploading a lone .gcode put the file on the card and the printer ignored every start command. '3mf' wraps it the way the printer expects (and uploads ~8x smaller, since g-code compresses well). 'gcode' is the old bare upload if a firmware ever prefers it. The .3mf is written next to the .gcode in the output folder, so it can be copied to a USB stick if the network dies.
lan._debug_comment: Prints every command we publish and every non-routine message the printer sends back. Turn this on when a file reaches the SD card but will not start — it is the only way to see what the printer is actually being told and what it answers.
lan._start_comment: Only consulted for container 'gcode', where firmware disagrees about the path prefix and the command name: 'auto' tries each shape in order and keeps the one the printer visibly acts on, waiting startProbeMs between tries. A 3mf has exactly one start command (project_file), so nothing is probed. project_file carries bed_leveling/flow_cali false as print-task parameters.
lan._clear_comment: A Bambu that has failed or finished a print keeps holding it: gcode_state stays FAILED, it goes on naming the dead job, and it refuses every new print command until told to let go — with the same err_code whatever you send, which is why this looked like a protocol fault for weeks. The booth sends the printer's own 'stop' before each job and waits this long for it to return to idle.

fan._comment: Part-cooling fan (0-255). Off on the first layer so it sticks, on for the rest - printing with no cooling causes drooping and stringing.
